p1_b0.ocr: The analysis of maternal serum selenium levels provides critical insights into the nutritional status of expectant mothers and its potential implications for both maternal and fetal health. In the presented data, the parameters of interest include the serum selenium concentrations measured in nanograms per milliliter (ng/ml) across two distinct groups: patients and controls. The mean serum selenium levels for the patient group ranged from 89.5 to 128 ng/ml, while the control group exhibited a slightly higher range of 92 to 131 ng/ml.

p1_b1.ocr: This observation raises important questions regarding the nutritional differences or health conditions prevalent in each cohort. Furthermore, the P-value of 0.08 suggests a trend towards significance in the comparison of selenium levels between the two groups; however, it falls short of conventional thresholds typically used to denote statistical significance. These findings underscore the necessity for further investigation into the role of selenium in maternal health and its potential influence on pregnancy outcomes. Understanding these dynamics could inform nutritional guidelines and intervention strategies aimed at optimizing maternal and fetal well-being.
